messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: increment_log_prob warning in BUGS/rats example
parts:
I am trying to understand and restructure the examples from BUGS following the new guidelines. The example from

https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/blob/master/bugs_examples/vol1/rats/rats_vec_unit.stan

gives an increment_log_prob warning, even if the results look ok. I tend to discard this version anyway, but first I would like to understand what the rationale behind the col(y,t) was.

model {
  mu_alpha ~ normal(0,1);
  mu_beta ~ normal(0,1);
  sigmasq_y ~ inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001);
  sigmasq_alpha ~ inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001);
  sigmasq_beta ~ inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001);
  alpha_z ~ normal(0, 1);
  beta_z ~ normal(0,1);
  for (t in 1:T)
    col(y,t) ~ normal(alpha + beta * (x[t] - xbar), sigma_y);

}


DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Warning (non-fatal):
 Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) may contain a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
If so, you need to call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
Left-hand-side of sampling statement:
    col(y,t) ~ normal(...)

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: increment_log_prob warning in BUGS/rats example
parts: Yeah this warning can just be ignored since col(y, t) is just  column t of the y matrix and not a transformation of a parameter. It's just a false positive.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] increment_log_prob warning in BUGS/rats example
parts:
I think the right thing to do is to update the data definition. Instead of:
   matrix[N,T] y;
we might declare this as:
   vector[T] y[N];

Yeah this warning can just be ignored since col(y, t) is just  column t of the y matrix and not a transformation of a parameter. It's just a false positive.

with

> vector[N] y[T]

relative to

> matrix[N,T] y;

but it'll be more efficient to index on T.
